<description>
Note: planned to be reworked, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36429#issuecomment-6315408546

Minimal implementation for "Delayed Transaction Broadcast" new feature.

Goal: Allow a user to submit a transaction for delayed broadcasting, that will be broadcast only later, at a randomized time. The aim is increased privacy, by making time-correlation-based tracking more difficult.
This fits together with private broadcast: private connection broadcast tries to hide the originator node; randomized delay tries to hide the creation time.

Goals in this PR: Extend the `sendrawtransaction` RPC with an optional `delay_for` parameter, and if set, postpone the initial broadcast to that later time, with some extra jitter.

Use case Details, with the limitations of the current changeset:
- What is a typical delay time? 30 - 90 minutes. (Too long times can get problematic: risk fee increase, node restart.)
- Delayed broadcast is only supported with private broadcast.
- Delay option and time is specified per submission (in `sendrawtransaction`). Alternative: with node level config.
- For now pending transactions are NOT persisted, so pending transactions will be lost during a node stop/restart/crash.
- Randomized delay is expressed as a percentage of the requested delay. A hard-coded value of 50% is used.
- Delay times are capped: requested delay between 0min to 12 hours, randomization range to minimum 5 minutes.
- Validation happens both at submission and broadcast time.
- No special handling for sudden fee increase situations.
- Pending (submitted but not yet broadcast) transactions can be inspected via existing `getprivatebroadcastinfo` RPC.
- The (pre-existing) `abortprivatebroadcast` RPC can be used to cancel a pending transaction submission.
- No special `nLockTime` handling, to be refined later.
- No special support from the wallet subsystem. (A submitted but not broadcast transactions is not visible in the wallet.)

Solution Details:
- The solution is based on the Private Broadcast implementation.
- Transactions are stored in the already-existing `m_transactions` collection.
- A scheduled periodic check is added to check for transactions that have became due. The implementation is very similar to the existing retry logic (`ReattemptPrivateBroadcast`).
- Queue is not persisted currently, to be added later.

Related issue: #34118
</description>

[2026-10-21] c:6308429903 comment by vasild (member):
[quoted text omitted]

Yes, I like this idea - use `nLockTime` for deciding when to send the transaction. Because:

* If a transaction is sent before the `nLockTime` height is reached, then it cannot confirm, so it does not make sense to send it earlier.
* If a transaction is sent after the `nLockTime` height is reached, then it trivially reveals when the transaction was created (`nLockTime`) and a delayed send will not hide it. So it does not make sense from privacy perspective.

[quoted text omitted]
If the point is to hide the transaction creation time and the wallet puts current height for `nLockTime` (like the Bitcoin Core wallet mostly does) then sending later does not make sense. So such an option could mislead users that they can hide the transaction creation time by using it?
[2026-10-21] c:6315408546 comment by optout21 (contributor) (edited 2026-10-21):
Following some recent discussions, I plan to do some changes to the feature:

- Acknowledge the two separate sub use cases of scheduling (for convenience) and random delay (for time obfuscation).

- Use the 'nLockTime' of the transaction as a basis for scheduling time, instead of an extra parameter. This way it can be ensured that the scheduling time and lock time are in sync (or if they are not, that's intended).

- Drop the random delay computation, because (1) it's not compatible with the lock time usage of the previous point, and (2) it is easy to be done on the client side

Keeping in Draft status until the above changes are applied.
[2026-10-21] c:6315555722 comment by optout21 (contributor):
[quoted text omitted]

@vasild , thanks for this and previous feedback! I also arrived at the same conclusion, see the previous comment.

I am thinking to also support the option for using a past lock time for obfuscation (wallet fingerprinting). One idea I came up with:

- In `sendrawtransaction` RPC introduce a new parameter `delay_after_lock_time`
- If not set, there is no delay
- If set (usually to 0), the delay is the sum of `nLockTime` and the parameter value

Examples (assume current height is 1000:
-  The wish is to broadcast only at height 1005: set lock time to 1005, and `delay_after_lock_time=0`
- The wish is to broadcast only at height 1005, but lock time set to 985: set lock time to 985, and `delay_after_lock_time=20`. Broadcast will be delayed until height 1005 (985+20).

Scheme to be refined. It should also support time-based lock time.
</new_statements>
